Physiology
P1: Electrophysiology of Heart
1. Influx of which of the following ions contributes most to maintaining the plateau in a
ventricular myocyte action potential?
A) Calcium
B) Sodium
C) Potassium
D) Chloride
Answer: A
2. In this SA node action potential, which channel is responsible for the phase marked by the Arrow?
A) Decrease in conductance of T-type calcium channels
B) Decrease in conductance of L-type calcium channel
C) Increase in conductance through fast Na+ channels
D) Increase in conductance through funny current Na+ channels
E) Increase conductance through K+ channel
Answer: D

3. During phase 4 of the ventricular action potential which ion is the plasma membrane most permeable
to?
A) K+
B) Na+
C) Cl￾D) Ca2+
Answer: A
4. Which of the following movements of ions across the surface membrane of the ventricular muscle cell
is responsible for the plateau phase (phase 2) of the ventricular muscle? (Use the diagram in question 3)
A) Sodium and potassium influx
B) Calcium influx and potassium efflux
C) Calcium efflux and potassium influx
D) Sodium influx and Calcium efflux
E) Sodium efflux and calcium influx
Answer: B (refer to the diagram above)

5. What is the effect of the sympathetic nervous system on the action potential of SA
node?
A) Shallower phase 4
B) Shallower phase 3
C) Steeper phase 4
Answer: C
6. What ion channels are responsible for the part of the graph with the arrow?
A) Opening of L-type Ca2+ channel and closing of delayed K+ channel.
B) Closing of L type Ca2+ channel and opening of delayed rectifier K+ channel.
C) Opening of T-type Ca2+ channel and closing of delayed K+ channel.
D) Opening of a funny current channel and closing of a delayed K+ channel.
Answer: B
7. Which of the following currents initiates the slow depolarization (phase 4) of sinoatrial node cells?
A) Funny current
B) L-type calcium channels
C) T-type calcium channels
D) Fast sodium channels
Answer: A

8. Early repolarization (phase 1) of the ventricular action potential is caused by which of the following
membrane currents?
A) Fast sodium current
B) Rapid potassium current
C) Delayed potassium current
D) Calcium current
E) Inward rectifier (background) potassium current
Answer: B
9. A person had a surgery where he got a pacemaker. Which of the following has been most likely
substituted?
A) AV node
B) SA node
C) Purkinje
Answer: B
10. Prolonged phase 4 of the Slow response of the SA nodal Pathway will cause which of the following?
A) Increased rate of ventricular contractions
B) Increased rate of Atrial contractions
C) No net change
D) Decreased rate of Atrial Contractions
Answer: D
11. What will happen if purkinje fibers are not functional?
A) Decreased atrial contraction
B) Tachycardia
C) Increasingly slowed ventricular contraction
D) Prominent QRS complexes on an ECG
Answer: C

12. Which of the following channels is present in Nodal cells , ventricular and purkinje.
A) Inward Rectifier
B) Delayed Rectifier Channel
C) T-type channels
D) Ito channels
Answer: B
14. What is the effect of ACh on the heart?
A) Increase heart rate
B) Decrease heart rate 
C) No change in heart rate 
D) Double the stroke volume
Answer: B
15. If the sinus node stops discharging, what is the expected heart rate (in beats/minute) if the A-V node
takes over as the cardiac pacemaker? (repeated)
A) 15
B) 20
C) 35
D) 50
E) 72
Answer: D (keep in mind that AV node rate is 40–60/min, so any number within this range should be
acceptable)

16. What ion is responsible for phase 0?
A) Sodium (Na⁺)
B) Potassium (K⁺)
C) Calcium (Ca²⁺)
D) Chloride (Cl⁻)
Answer: C
17. What happens in phase 1 of the cardiomyocyte AP?
A) Sodium channels open, causing a rapid influx of sodium ions
B) Calcium channels open, creating a prolonged plateau phase
C) Sodium channels close, and voltage-gated potassium channels open
D) Potassium channels close, allowing the cell to return to its resting potential
Answer: C

18. Which phase of the ventricular action potential coincides with diastole? (see attached figure)
A) Phase 0
B) Phase 1
C) Phase 2
D) Phase 3
E) Phase 4
Answer: E
19. The conduction pathway through the heart is the fastest in which of the following
structures? (repeated)
A) Purkinje fibers
B) Bundle branches
C) Sinoatrial node
D) Bundle of his
E) Atrioventricular node
Answer: A
20. If someone has a complete AV block on ECG, what is the heart rate? (Repeated)
A) 92
B) 40
C) 60
D) 70
Answer: B
21. A patient presents to the emergency department and is found to have a sinoatrial (SA) block. Which
of the following is the most likely heart rate for this patient?
A) 45 bpm
B) 72 bpm
C) 110 bpm

D) 100 bpm
E) 90 bpm
Answer: A
22. What occurs at the SA node to decrease heart rate?
A) Increased permeability of Sodium
B) Increased permeability of Calcium
C) Decreased permeability of Potassium
D) Increased ACh
E) Increased Norepinephrine
Answer: D
23. How long does it take for the impulse to travel from the SA node to the beginning of the purkinje
fiber? (the P-R interval)
A) 0.35s
B) 0.80s
C) 0.16s
D) 0.03s
Answer: C
24. Which of the following inhibits the SA node?
A) High levels of norepinephrine
B) High levels of acetylcholine
C) Increased calcium permeability
Answer: B
25. If the AV node is the pacemaker of the heart, what would be the heart rate? (repeated)
A) 55 beats/min
B) 75 beats/min
C) 100 beats/min
D) 20 beats/min
Answer: A (keep in mind that AV node rate is 40–60/min, so any number within this range should be
acceptable)

26. The rate of AV node discharge/excitation is decreased by: (repeated)
A) Increased acetylcholine levels
B) Increased norepinephrine levels
C) Increased sodium permeability
D) Increased calcium permeability
E) Decreased potassium permeability
Answer: A 
27. If the S-A node discharges at 0.00 seconds, when will the action potential normally arrive at the
septum?
A) 0.22 sec
B) 0.25 sec
C) 0.16 sec
D) 0.12 sec
E) 0.09 sec
Answer: C
28. Which of the following increases the firing of action potentials at the SA node?
A) Increased norepinephrine
B) Increased acetylcholine.
C) Increased K+ conductance
D) Decreased Ca2+ conductance
E) Decreased Na+ conductance
Answer: A
29. During phase 4 of the ventricular action potential, which ion is the plasma membrane most
permeable to?
A) Potassium
B) Magnesium
C) Chloride
D) Calcium
E) Sodium
Answer: A

P2: Excitation - Contraction Coupling
1. Which of the following does calcium bind to when cardiac muscles contract?
A) Troponin C
B) Tropomyosin
C) Calmodulin
D) Myosin light chain kinase
Answer: A 
2. During relaxation of cardiac muscle (diastole) which of the following proteins contributes the most to
the decline of cytosolic calcium?
A) Sarcoendoplasmic calcium ATPase
B) Sodium/calcium exchange
C) Plasmalemmal calcium ATPase
D) Calmodulin
Answer: A
3. During dilated cardiomyopathy, the intercalated discs will be dysfunctional. Which of the following
will happen?
A) SA node will speed up
B) AV node will speed up
C) Purkinje fibers degenerate
D) Cardiac output increases
E) Gap junctions will stop spreading action potential
Answer: E
4. Which of the following hydrolyses the most ATP in ventricular cells ?
A) Myosin Atpase
B) SERCA2 atpase
C) Sarcolemmal ATP-ase
D) Sodium-Potassium Pump
Answer: A

5. Frank–Starling law states the:
A) Relation between cardiac output and end-diastolic volume
B) Relation between venous return and end-systolic volume
Answer: A
6. Which of the following best describes the function of intercalated discs in a cardiac myocyte?
A) Give structural support
B) Allow faster electrical conductance
C) Hold muscle cells together more tightly
Answer: B/C
7. What is the most characteristic feature of the ventricular conduction system?
A) Small diameter
B) Presence of intercalated disc
C) Striation is visible in all sarcoplasm
Answer: B
8. If the Ca level decreased in cytoplasm right before relaxation, what has caused the decrease in the level
of Ca?
A) RyR2 ( ryanodine channel )
B) L - type channel
C) Voltage-gated Ca²⁺ channel
D) Na/Ca exchange
Answer: D
9. What part of the intercalated disc transmits low electrical resistance through which excitation passes
from one cell to the other? 
A) Desmosomes
B) Fascia adherens
C) Gap junctions
D) Tight junctions
Answer: C

P3: ECG I
(Note: some questions are highlighted as they are relevant to the slides though are unexplained in the lecture)
1. What is the length of the PR segment in the following ECG?
A) 0.12
B) 0.04
C) 0.16
D) 0.20
E) 0.24
Answer: B
2. The negative electrode of lead II is placed on the:
 A) Right arm
 B) Left leg
 C) Left arm
Answer: A
3. When recording lead III on an ECG, the negative electrode is the:
A) Left arm
B) Left leg
C) Right leg
D) Left arm left leg
E) Right arm left leg
Answer: A
4. By using the einthoven law, the lead I voltage was 0.4 and lead II voltage was 0.9, which of the
following would be the voltage of lead III?
A) 0.5
B) 0.6

C) 0.7
D) 0.8
E) 0.9
Answer: A
5. If in an ECG, the voltage at lead I is 0.8 mV and the voltage at lead II is 1.2 mV, what is the voltage at
lead III?
 A) 0.70 mV
 B) 2.0 mV
 C) 0.40 mV
 Answer: C
6. What stage in the ECG corresponds to total ventricular depolarization?
A) 1
B) 2
C) 3
D) 4
E) 5
F) 6
Answer: D

7. In a normal ECG, Which of the following is correct?
A) PR interval is > 0.2s
B) ST segment represents the duration of ventricular action potential
C) T wave represents ventricular repolarization
D) Duration of the QRS complex is 1 sec
E) R-R interval represents atrial depolarization
Answer: C
8. Which of the following leads will have a strong negative QRS complex for the following depolarizing
signal?
A) AVL, V6
B) Lead 1, AVF
C) Lead 2, AVF
D) Lead 3,V2
Answer: A

9. During which wave or segment on the ECG trace below marks ventricular depolarization?
A) A
B) B
C) C
D) E
Answer: C
10. Which component of the ECG is the result of a conduction of a wave of depolarization through the
atrial muscle?
A) PR interval
B) P wave
C) QRS complex
D) ST segment
E) T wave
Answer: B
11. Which of the following will be a result of the direct consequences of slowing the action potential
conduction to the AV node?
A) Increased cardiac output
B) QRS complex will be prolonged
C) QT interval will be shortened
D) PR interval will be prolonged
Answer: D

12. You are looking at an ECG of a patient whose MEA is +60°, which lead would have
an S wave with the biggest amplitude? (Not included in 19th batch curriculum)
A) Lead I
B) Lead III
C) aVF
D) aVR
E) aVL
Answer: D
13. General impulse travels towards apex which leads to the tallest positive
QRS?
A) Lead 1
B) Lead 2
C) aVF
D) aVL
E) Lead 3
Answer: B
14. The ECG tracing shown below was taken from a patient during a routine examination. What is the
best estimate of heart rate taken from this ECG record in beats per minute (bpm)?
A) 30
B) 50
C) 70
D) 90
Answer: B

15. Which of the following is in the normal time range for the PR segment?
A) 0.08
B) 0.2
C) 0.16
D) 0.24
Answer: A
16. Sympathetic nerve stimulation of AV node increases conduction velocity through the node. Which of
the following is likely to decrease because of this intervention?
A) Heart rate
B) PR interval on ECG
C) Metabolic demands
D) Coronary flow rate
E) Cardiac Contractility
Answer: B
17. Where is the negative electrode of Lead I attached?
A) Left arm
B) Right arm
C) Left leg
D) Right leg
Answer: B
18. If Lead III = 0.4 mV and Lead II = 0.9 mV, what is Lead I?
A) 0.5 mV
B) 1.3 mV
C) 0.12 mV
D) 0.05 mV
Answer: A
19. Where do you put the positive electrode of lead 1?
A) Left Arm
B) Right Arm 
C) Left Leg

D) Left Arm and Left Leg 
Answer: A
20. If in an ECG, the voltage at lead 1 is 0.8 and the voltage at lead 3 is 0.4, what is the voltage at lead 2?
A) 0.4
B) 1.2
C) 0.32
D) 0.12
Answer: B
21. The probability of the random desynchronization of the myocardium is highest when the electrical
signal arrives at the myocardium during the vulnerable phase of the cardiac cycle. This phase
corresponds with which of the following waves on the electrocardiogram (ECG)?
A) P
B) S
C) Q
D) R
E) T
Answer: E
Q22.Which of the following is the normal time of the P-R interval?
A) 0.35s
B) 0.60s
C) 0.24s
D) 0.12s
E) 0.16s
Answer: E (While the normal range of PR interval is 0.12 – 0.20s , 0.16s is considered the average PR
interval in standard medical and physiology textbooks. Question could be double keyed for D and E)

23. Which labelled portion [1 to 5] of the ECG diagram in the attachment represents
ventricular depolarization?
A) 1
B) 2
C) 3
D) 4
E) 5
Answer: C

P4: ECG II (Arrhythmias)
1.What does the following ECG indicate?
A) 1st degree heart block
B) 2nd degree heart block type 1
C) 2nd degree heart block type 2
D) 3rd degree heart block
E) Sinus bradycardia
Answer: E
2. From the ECG shown, which is the most likely condition in this patient?
A) Sinus bradycardia
B) Junctional rhythm
C) 3rd-degree heart block
D) 2nd degree type 1
E) 2nd degree type 2
Answer: C
3. What is the heart condition in the following ecg?

A) Second-degree heart block (Mobitz type I)
B) First-degree heart block
C) Third-degree heart block
D) Second-degree heart block (Mobitz type II)
Answer: B
4. From the attached ECG trace, what is the most likely condition affecting this patient?
A) First degree heart block
B) Second degree heart block (Type I)
C) Sinus tachycardia
D) Second degree heart block (Type II)
E) Atrial fibrillation
Answer: C

5. A patient experiences a cardiac arrhythmia and presents with the following ECG, what is the diagnosis
of his condition?
A) First degree AV Block
B) Paroxysmal Ventricular Tachycardia
C) SA Block
D) Third Degree AV Block (Complete AV block)
Answer: D
6. A 42 year old woman complained of palpitations, her ECG is shown here. Which of the following best
describes her ECG?
A) Regularly Irregular
B) Normally regular
C) Regularly regular
D) Irregularly irregular
Answer: A

7. From the attached ECG, what is the most likely condition affecting this patient?
A) Junctional Rhythm
B) Sinus Bradycardia
C) Third-degree heart block
D) Second-degree heart block (Type II)
E) Second-degree heart block (Type I)
Answer: C
P5: Interactive Session I
1. Which of the following is most likely to cause ventricular fibrillation?
A) Increased K+ in ECF
B) Increased Cardiac Output
C) Sympathetic stimulation
D) Exercise
E) Complete repolarization of the membrane
Answer: A
P6: Cardiac Cycle
1. What does slow ventricular ejection correspond to on an ECG? (Repeated)

A) T wave
B) QRS complex
C) P wave
D) ST segment
E) PR interval
Answer: A
2. During exercise the cardiac cycle is shortened. Shortening of which of the following phases is mostly
responsible for this? (Repeated)
A) Rapid ventricular filling
B) Isovolumetric contraction
C) Isovolumetric relaxation
D) Slow ventricular filling
Answer: D
3. You are listening to a patient's heart sounds while simultaneously recalling the cardiac cycle events.
Which of the following most likely occurs at the same time as the S2 heart sound?
A) Left ventricular volume reaches its maximum value
B) Left ventricular pressure reaches its maximum value
C) The dicrotic notch in the aortic pressure valve
D) Aortic pressure approaches its minimum value
E) Rapid ventricular ejection
Answer: C
4. Ejection fraction is 0.8, ESV is 30 mL, and heart rate is 100 bpm. Calculate the cardiac output in
L/min.
A) 11
B) 12
C) 13
D) 14
Answer: B
5. What is the difference in ejection between the right and left cardiac components of the heart?
A) Right side ejects less amount of blood.
B) Right side ejects slower than left
C) Right side ejects against a lower afterload
D) Left side ejects against lower afterload

Answer: C
6. Which of the following represents the ventricular ejection phase?
A) 3
B) 4
C) 5
D) 1
E) 2
Answer: A
7. Which correctly pairs an ECG wave with the corresponding cardiac event?
A) P-wave: Depolarization of the ventricles
B) P-wave: Depolarization of the AV node
C) QRS-wave: Depolarization of the ventricles
D) QRS-wave: Repolarization of the ventricles
E) T-wave: Repolarization of the atria
Answer: C
8. Calculate the ejection fraction if the End diastolic volume is 200 and end
systolic volume is 150?
A) 50%
B) 25%

C) 75%
D) 10%
Answer: B
9. A patient with valve disease undergoes cardiac catheterization to compare vascular and intracardiac
pressures for comparison with normal values. Which of the following is found in a normal heart?
A) Aortic diastolic pressure is less than pulmonary artery systole pressure
B) Right atrial pressure is greater than left atrial pressure
C) Mean systolic aortic pressure is less than aortic diastolic pressure
D) Pulmonary artery diastolic pressure is greater than right atrial pressure
Answer: D
10. What causes the “a” wave in the jugular waveform?
A) Atrial relaxation
B) Closure of the tricuspid valve
C) Atrial contraction
D) Filling of right atrium
Answer: C
11. What is mostly correlated after the QRS complex on an ECG?
A) Rapid Ventricular Filling
B) Slow Ventricular Filling
C) Isovolumetric Contraction
D) Isovolumetric Relaxation
Answer: C
12. During which phase of the cardiac cycle does the mitral valve open?
A) Atrial systole
B) End of volumetric ventricular contraction
C) Rapid ventricular ejection
D) End of volumetric ventricular relaxation
E) Slow ventricular ejection
Answer: D

P7: Ventricular PV Loops
1. At what point does rapid ventricular ejection start?
A) A
B) B
C) C
D) D
E) E
Answer: C
2. Calculate the Ejection fraction for the following PV loop.

A) 0.33
B) 0.65
C) 0.72
D) 0.85
Answer: B
3. In the attached PV loop, isovolumic relaxation begins at which of the following points?
A) A
B) B
C) C
D) D
Answer: D
4. How does the sympathetic nervous system affect the heart?

A) Decrease end-systolic volume
B) Decrease stroke volume
C) Decrease heart rate
D) Decrease systemic pressure
Answer: A
5. If the contractility increases, which of the following parameters will decrease in the PV loop?
A) Stroke volume
B) Stroke work
C) Pressure difference from point D to A
D) End systolic volume
E) End systolic pressure volume relationship slope
Answer: D
6. What change occurred to move the solid PV loop to the dashed one?

A) Decreased contractility
B) Increased End-diastolic volume
C) Decreased EDV
D) Increased ESV
E) Decreased ESV
Answer: E
7. What happens at point D on the cardiac output curve?
A) Aortic valve closes
B) Aortic valve opens
C) AV valve opens
D) AV valve closes
Answer: A
8. Which of the following increases Stroke Volume?

A) Increased Afterload
B) Decreased Preload
C) Increased EDV
D) Decreased Contractility
Answer: C
9. A 50-year-old man has a body weight of 110 kg, resting heart rate is 90 beats/min, arterial pressure
120/70 and normal body temperature. His pressure volume diagram of the left ventricle is shown in the
figure. What event occurs at point A? 
A) AV valves close
B) Aortic valve opens
C) Third heart sound
D) AV valves open
E) Aortic valves opens
Answer: D
10. What happens at the beginning of the isovolumetric relaxation?
A) Aortic valve opens
B) Mitral valve closes
C) Mitral valve opens
D) Aortic valve closes
Answer: D
11. Between which interval does the ventricle fills?

A) From A to B
B) From B to C
C) From C to D
D) From D to A
Answer: A
12. What change occurred to move the solid PV loop to the dashed one?
